research_question: What is the effect of indicated interventions compared with control on suicidal ideation measured immediately postintervention among young people up to age 25 in education settings?
outcome_description: Suicidal ideation measured immediately at postintervention (end of intervention)
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates greater reduction in suicidal ideation in the indicated intervention group compared to the control group (favoring intervention)
search_queries: indicated suicide intervention school college youth trial
indicated intervention suicidal ideation students randomized controlled
targeted suicide prevention young people education setting trial
inclusion_criteria: Empirical studies evaluating an indicated intervention targeting youth or young adults (up to age 25) with existing suicidal ideation, self-harm history, or early risk signs in an education setting (e.g., middle/high school, college, university)
Comparison of the indicated intervention against a control group (e.g., treatment-as-usual, waitlist, attention control, or minimal intervention)
Quantitative assessment of suicidal ideation measured immediately at the end of the intervention (postintervention)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, commentaries, or theoretical papers)

Universal or purely selective interventions that do not target symptomatic/at-risk youth showing early signs or suicidal ideation/self-harm history, or studies outside education settings / with mean age > 25
No comparison between an indicated intervention and a control condition, or lack of quantitative suicidal ideation data at postintervention to calculate an effect size
Completely unrelated to suicide prevention interventions among young people
moderators_to_extract: Control condition type (waitlist, treatment-as-usual, attention/active control)
Intervention duration or number of sessions
effect_size_note: Extract each indicated intervention arm separately against shared control in multi-arm trials. If sample size per group is unreported in a randomized trial, assume a 50/50 split between arms and document this assumption.
